label: GO after a reward, when the agent is confidently choosing a1, mid-episode (trials ~20-79)
explanation: Fires almost only at GO (99.9% of mass); never at D2 and essentially never at D1. It needs three things together: the previous trial was rewarded (prev_reward=1 holds 99.9% of mass, 0 on unrewarded), the agent is about to choose a1 with a very confident policy (choice logit a1-a2 in its top bin >8.07 holds 99.7% of mass; a2 choices never fire; in practice this is usually a stay on a1 after a rewarded a1 trial while S1 is good), and the trial falls in the middle of the episode: zero activity on episode trials 0-19 and 80-99, with a peak at trials 30-69. That episode-time window suggests the unit is also gated by a slow internal clock in the hidden state. Scored only on observed or self-computed variables (the previous reward, the agent own policy logit, episode time); no FUTURE variables. The upcoming action==1 works in place of choice>8.07 but is less precise (dev F1 0.71 against 0.84). Magnitude: in the example windows the activation shrinks slowly over a run of consecutive rewarded a1 GO steps (for example 0.66, 0.63, 0.60, 0.55, 0.48), and the strongest activations come at GO right after a reward, often on the first rewarded trial after unrewarded ones. Remaining false positives (precision about 0.73) are GO steps that meet every condition but stay below threshold, mostly late in a long reward streak.

issues: The episode-time window is set wrong, and this produces a systematic false-positive class. Inside the predicate's conditions (GO, prev_reward=1, choice>8.07): ep_trial 75-79 has dev precision 0.071 (4670 predicted, only about 330 active), so it supplies about 28% of all dev false positives. Trials 20-24 have precision 0.495. The unit's real window is about trials 22-74, not 20-79, and the label's 'trials ~20-79' should change to match.

The remaining false positives look like threshold noise on a graded signal, not a new class. Precision is about 0.72 in every slice: good state S1, S2 or unknown; prev_common; prev_action. It rises only with a larger choice logit (choice>9: precision 0.81) or a narrower time window (30-69: 0.86). So both the choice and time conditions are graded, and the explanation's 'meets every condition but stays below threshold' is roughly right.

The factual claims mostly hold up. Mass shares: GO 99.9%, D2 0, D1 65 steps; prev_reward=1 99.9%; top choice bin 99.7%. Only 69 active steps have action==2. The time effect holds even with the choice condition fixed: the predicate restricted to ep_trial<20 or >=80 has precision 0.006 and mass 0.000. 'Zero activity on trials 0-19' is a small overclaim: dev has 163 active steps in trials 10-19, with negligible mass.

The claim that rewarded GO steps with prev_reward=0 don't fire is confirmed: (GO & prev_reward==0 & choice>8.07 & mid-episode) has precision 0.004. The 'staying on a1 after a rewarded a1 trial' wording is fine: prev_action==2 adds nothing, and the other ~24% of recall is window-first trials where prev_action is unknown.
The reported scores reproduce: test P 0.708, R 0.987, F1 0.824. Test misses are only 519 steps (0.4% of mass), all scattered weak activations, so there is no systematic miss class.

Better predicate: (phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & (choice > 8.5) & (ep_trial >= 22) & (ep_trial < 75). Test P 0.817, R 0.945, F1 0.876, mass recall 0.982, against the original's test F1 0.824. With the time bounds alone fixed (choice > 8.07, trials 22-74), test F1 is 0.863.
